overall_structure.value: Disordered / short-range-ordered Fe–20% Al (+0.1% B) after 2–3% room-temperature compression: plasticity is carried by singly gliding (1/2)⟨111⟩ dislocations that are generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations, showing a weak tendency to cluster into an incipient cell structure, and with many of the segments being dipoles together with occasional small dipole loops.

source.reason: b0031 (Section 3.2) presents the dislocation structures as a function of Al content, describing the disordered/short-range-ordered 15–20% Al materials; Figs. 5–7 illustrate the 15 and 20% Al materials. These describe the 20% Al composition class of this sample.

unmapped_findings: The dislocation-structure micrographs and descriptions for the low-Al-content material (Figs. 5–7 and b0031) are labelled 'Fe–20% Al' / 'materials containing 15 and 20% Al' and do not explicitly state the 0.1% B content; they have been assigned here to the 20% Al composition class that includes this sample, but they may correspond to the binary Fe–20% Al composition.

Fig. 1 gives the yield stress and ductility of polycrystalline Fe–Al alloys versus Al content but does not distinguish the B-containing alloy; at 20% Al the ductility is about 25% and the yield stress increases steadily up to 25% Al, but no specific value is reported for the 20% Al + 0.1% B sample.

The work hardening rate peak (maximum measured over the 1–1.5% strain range) occurs in the 26–29% Al range (near 29% Al) for the ordered Fe–Al alloys; the 20% Al material lies on the low disordered plateau of the work hardening curve (Fig. 2).
The cast ingot grain size for all alloys in the study is of the order of 0.25 mm (b0022).
